newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin sacks minister, appoints him as governor.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin sacks minister, appoints him as governor.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin sacked communist Aman Tuleyev on Tuesday as Russia's Minister for Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) Affairs and appointed him governor of Siberia's Kemerovo region.

Yeltsin's press service said in a statement that the governor of the coal-mining Kemerovo region, Mikhail Kislyuk, had been transferred to another post, making way for Tuleyev. The Kremlin has not yet named Tuleyev's successor as CIS affairs minister.
Tuleyev had previously been governor of Kemerovo but was dismissed by Yeltsin in 1991 for supporting a coup against then Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev.
Under Russia's constitution, Yeltsin is entitled to appoint regional governors. However all Russian regions except Kemerovo have now held governorship elections.

Tuleyev was brought into the government last August as minister for relations with the CIS, a loose grouping of former Soviet republics. As a minister, he has been critical of the government's reformist course.

Tuleyev is a popular figure in the Kemerovo region, where he used to head the local assembly before joining the government. The region is due to hold a governorship poll in October and Tuleyev's chances are high, political analysts say.

He ran for the Russian presidency twice. Last year Tuleyev was an understudy of Communist leader Gennady Zyuganov but withdrew from the race in Zyuganov's favour. He came fourth with seven percent of the vote in Russia's 1991 presidential election, which Yeltsin won by a landslide.
Kislyuk, whose popularity in the region has been low recently, has also criticised the government and supported coalminers' protests over unpaid wages.
Russia's First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais blasted the region's administration last week for inadequate tax and insurance collection.
